The paper proposes a general analytical method to study electromagnetic wave interactions with a radially anisotropic spherical cloak.
The cloak structure consists of an inner isotropic dielectric region, an intermediate radially anisotropic metamaterial cloak region, and an outer host medium.
The paper discretizes the anisotropic cloak shell into multiple homogeneous anisotropic spherical layers to derive a general scattering solution.
The general cloaking condition is derived as a relation between the evolution operator of the cloak shell and the impedance tensor of the 'virtual' air sphere.
The nonlinear transformation-based (NTB) spherical cloaks use a nonlinear radial transformation function to determine the anisotropic material parameters.
The optimal range of the nonlinearity parameter 'x' for the NTB cloaks is found to be around 2, where they outperform the classic linear Pendry cloak.
The transverse permittivity of the NTB cloak shell exhibits a non-monotonic behavior along the radial direction in the optimal range of 'x'.
The paper shows that the NTB cloaks can provide improved invisibility performance over a wider range of scattering angles compared to the linear Pendry cloak.
The authors discretize the inhomogeneous anisotropic cloak shell into N = 50 homogeneous anisotropic layers for their numerical simulations.
The radial permittivity of the NTB cloaks is found to be quite close to that of the Pendry cloak, but the transverse permittivity exhibits more complex behavior.
The paper demonstrates that the scattering cross-section of the NTB cloaks can be lower than that of the Pendry cloak over a certain range of the nonlinearity parameter 'x'.
The authors investigate how the variance of the transverse permittivity along the radial direction in the cloak shell changes with the nonlinearity parameter 'x'.
The paper shows that for 'x' slightly above 1, the requirement on the transverse permittivity near the inner boundary of the cloak shell drops significantly.
As 'x' becomes larger, the transverse permittivity at the outer boundary of the cloak shell deviates more from the corresponding radial permittivity.
The optimal range of 'x' corresponds to non-monotonic transverse permittivity profiles along the radial direction with smaller overall values.
